the scientific publication process has changed in a number of ways due to the Internet, that the changes have been studied in depth, but that the socio‐economic structures are still very much the same as before, and that the cost implications are still largely unknown.

a model of the scientific publications process has been developed, which is useful for studying the cost aspects of different business models, as well as for providing a roadmap for different types of Open Access initiatives.

the current scientific publication process can be described as a process with a number of steps, which can be described in a process model, and that the process model is a good tool to use in the analysis of different business models.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: how can a formalised model of a complex process be used to provide a basis of analysis and understanding of the process?
the development of an understanding of how to manage the scientific publishing process.
how to make the current system work more effectively.

the current situation is not satisfactory and that the current system needs to change.
the scientific publishing process has not been changed much by the advent of the Internet.
the model is a useful tool for studying the scholarly communication system, but that it is still too early to draw any firm conclusions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the model provides a solid basis for further work, both in cost studies and for understanding the implications of open access initiatives on the scientific publication process.
we have developed a formal model that is useful for describing the life‐cycle and costs of the publication process.
the model is an important tool for studying the cost of different models of scholarly communication.

the current system is highly complex and the changes that are needed to improve the system will be difficult to achieve.
it is not possible to make a generalised statement about whether the scientific publication process is more efficient now than it was before.
the current situation is not a simple matter of a transition between two models.
